events.text: A folding table in the middle of a corridor, laid with the sort of things you only find on a dead station: three coils of cable, a box of odd batteries, someone's good boots. Behind it sits {name} on an upturned crate, with a cashbox and an expression of mild professional hope. 'Don't touch the boots,' {name} says. 'The boots are not for sale. The boots are for looking at.'

outcomes.text: 'Three things,' says {name}. 'Pick one. Don't pick the boots.' The prices are written in grease pencil on the table, and corrected twice.
You and {name} haggle for nine minutes with real joy, like two cats dancing. {name} ends up parting with the cable for less than cost, and thanks you for the best afternoon since the Snap.
'Anyone who comes,' says {name}. 'It's been a slow year.' {name} laughs at that, once, and means about half of it. 'There's a box in the back. Tell it I sent you.'

choices.text: Admire the boots and move on.

outcomes.text: 'They're very good boots,' says {name}, to the corridor.

events.text: {name} has a battered shortwave set open on the table like a patient, and a kettle that has been boiling for so long the room has gone soft with it. 'Don't talk,' {name} says. 'It's about to come round.' You wait. After a while the speaker clears its throat and a small tired voice says, 'If you can hear this, we're alive,' and {name} mouths along with it, word for word, with the face of a person at a christening.

choices.text: Ask how long {name} has been listening.

outcomes.text: 'Since it started,' says {name}. 'Not every day. Some days I've a customer.' A dial is turned a hair, and the voice comes in cleaner. 'It's always late, did you notice? The real one's always late. If it ever comes on the minute I'm leaving a note and going the other way.' The set spits a second voice from far off: a signals desk, filing the same form again. {name} copies it down for you on the back of a receipt.
'Mostly valves,' says {name}. 'And a little of what valves pay for.'
The voice comes round again as you reach the door. {name} does not look up. {name} mouths it.

events.text: A stall, a lamp, a hand-lettered sign: BACK IN FIVE MINUTES. It is faded so far past five minutes that the ink has gone brown. {name} sits under it with a cashbox on one knee and a second chair set out beside the first, with a coat on it. 'My partner's coming back,' {name} says. 'They said five minutes.' It is said flatly, as a fact about the weather, and the two of you look at the chair.

choices.text: Sit in the other chair for five minutes.

outcomes.text: You sit, and wait, and nobody comes. At the end of the five minutes {name} stands up, folds the sign in half, then in quarters, and puts it in a pocket. 'Right,' {name} says. 'Right. That's that, then.' The coat goes into the cashbox. 'I'll need a berth, if you've got one. I can sell anything to anyone. It's the only thing I'm good for.'

You sit. Five minutes go by. {name} looks at the coat, then at you, then at the coat, and shakes a head. 'No,' {name} says. 'No, I'll wait a bit more.' It is not an unkind refusal. {name} sells you something quickly, to cover it.
'Thank you,' says {name}, with a customer's brightness, and doesn't look at the second chair at all.
You go. Behind you the lamp stays on.

events.text: {name} is taking stock, with a clipboard, of a heap that is mostly dust. 'Closing down,' {name} says. 'Everything must go.' There is no one else on the deck. There has been no one else for a while. {name} has a hat on, and the hat says MANAGER.

outcomes.text: 'Everything's a bargain,' says {name}. 'There's no one to argue.'

choices.text: Ask where the good stock went.

outcomes.text: 'Back room,' says {name}. 'Don't tell head office.' There is no head office. {name} knows it, and says it anyway.
'Sale ends Thursday,' says {name}. You do not ask which one.
